$comment: Store listing fields that apify push never sends. Applied by scripts/store-metadata.mjs after every deploy. Title, description and categories live in actor.json.
seoTitle: Domain History Lookup - WHOIS History + Past Owner Contacts
seoDescription: Domain history lookup API. Find who owned a domain in the past: WHOIS history, Wayback pages, and the owner's emails, phones and names, each with a source URL and date.

defaultRunOptions.$comment: 2 GB is efficient since the ONNX thread cap (Standard scan 351s, 0.195 CU). Memory x timeout is the compute ceiling the start fee must cover: 2 GB x 1800 s = 1 CU = $0.20 at the developer rate. A user who raises memory pays the start fee per GB, which scales with the higher ceiling.

pricing.$comment: First-time set, applied by CI when the platform has no pricing yet; afterwards Apify allows one change per 30 days, so later changes go through Console. Sizing: developer cost is $0.20 per CU (measured $0.205 on five runs); Quick scan $0.02, Standard $0.04, ceiling at the 2 GB / 1800 s defaults $0.20. The start event bills once per GB: 2 x $0.125 = $0.25 per run at defaults, of which the developer keeps 80% = $0.20, so a run that hits the full ceiling with nothing found still breaks even (the nmap lesson). Contacts and mentions are priced apart so a big corporate archive with 140 named universities does not cost the user $4 in mention rows. Do not add apify-default-dataset-item: rows are charged by the contact and mention events from code, and the summary row is free.

apify-actor-start.eventDescription: Charged once per GB of run memory when a scan starts: $0.25 at the default 2 GB. Covers the archive crawl, page rendering, the entity model, registration, DNS, certificate and reference lookups, and the coverage report, at any depth.

contact.eventDescription: One row per contact per source: an email, a phone number, a person or organisation that is part of the site, or a registrant detail from WHOIS history, certificates or public code. Each row carries the URL and capture date it came from.

mention.eventDescription: A person or organisation named in the site's content rather than part of the site, such as a company in a biography or a university in an article. Kept for context, priced at a tenth of a contact.
